look_here_first: Start with the tiny linear leaves. Narrowleaf elbowbush is densely twiggy with stiff 90-degree branching and very narrow leathery, often slightly rolled leaves. That skeletal, almost olive-like foliage separates it quickly from the broader-leaved F. pubescens.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub, drought-deciduous in severe dryness

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense intricate branching with stiff near-right-angle branchlets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins entire and often revolute

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: young twigs dark; older bark smooth gray

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: inconspicuous green-yellow apetalous flowers before new leaves

lookalikes.differences: F. pubescens has much broader elliptic/ovate leaves with more visible pubescence and a winter-deciduous habit; F. angustifolia is the narrow, skeletal-leaved shrub.
